writeup.key_factor: The model makes Milwaukee a 44.6% underdog (fair +124) — playoff-compressed Elo: Brewers 1574 vs Dodgers 1555 + 12 home field, with Blake Snell rated ace (+45) against Robert Gasser as a league-average arm (0; 3.87 ERA) — yet Caesars offers +150, implying only 40.0%. Milwaukee leads the NLCS 2-0 and is 9-1 in its last 10, Gasser owns a 2.50 ERA over his last 36 innings, and Snell's 2026 sample is just 42 innings — he walked five in 3.2 innings in his playoff start against Atlanta. The market is pricing Snell's small-sample form as certain; the model is not.
writeup.risk: Snell is an elite left-hander when healthy, and Los Angeles is desperate at home down 0-2 (52-31 at home this year). The edge is tier-sensitive: if Gasser is really a #4 arm (-20) instead of league-average, Milwaukee's win probability falls to about 41.8% and the edge shrinks to roughly +1.8%, below the program minimum. Milwaukee is also without Brandon Woodruff, Quinn Priester and Nick Zerpa (IL).

writeup.key_factor: The expanded full-FBS Elo — built on 450 real 2026 results, schedule-adjusted across all 138 FBS teams — rates Missouri State a slight favorite at home (52.9%, fair -112), while the market prices them off a 1-4 record on a five-game sample: Pinnacle's +119 implies just 45.7%. The gap is a small-sample record being priced as a talent gap, plus home field in Springfield that the market is not fully crediting.
writeup.risk: Thin samples on both sides (about five games each, both 1-4) and a rating scale compressed toward 1500 in the expansion — the 52.9% is a soft estimate, not a sharp one. This is the first G5 quote of the expanded coverage, and the market drifted the other way this afternoon: the price widened from +116 and the other books sit lower (+112 to +115) — respect the move, do not chase it shorter, and the +105 minimum stands.
